title: Scope, authority and exclusions for appliance cleaning
referencesAtStart: Official references for this lesson: Safe Work Australia, Managing the risks of plant in the workplace (model code of practice) (no date shown); Ozone Protection and Synthetic Greenhouse Gas Management Regulations 1995 (current compilation, in force from 1 July 2026); NSW Government, Electricians (last updated 1 December 2025); Energy Safe Victoria, Electrical workers (reviewed 24 January 2025); Energy Safe Victoria, Gasfitter licences (reviewed 18 August 2025); WorkSafe Queensland, Classes of electrical work licences (no date shown); Queensland Building and Construction Commission, Gasfitting (last published 2 November 2026; last reviewed 31 August 2021); Victorian BPC, Servicing Type A gas appliances (AS 4575) (no date shown); Electrical Licensing Board (WA), Electrical licensing (last updated 22 October 2026); WA Building and Energy, Having gasfitting work done (last updated 23 November 2024); Consumer and Business Services (SA), Plumbing, gas fitting or electrical contractors licence (no date shown); Tasmania CBOS, Electrical contractor licence (last updated 12 February 2025); NT WorkSafe, Electrical licensing contacts (no date shown); ACT Government, Electrician licence (no date shown); ACT Government, Gas appliance workers (no date shown). Only part of six of these sources has been confirmed: the Safe Work Australia plant code, the refrigerant licence offence in regulation 111, the Tasmania electrical contractor page, the NT electrical licensing contacts page, and the two ACT pages.
audience: Workers and supervisors who clean the outside and accessible parts of specialty appliances and machines, such as commercial dishwashers, ovens, fryers, coffee and ice machines, laundry machines and light workshop machines
learningOutcomes: Describe the external and accessible components that this course covers for each appliance type
Identify the work that is excluded because it needs a licensed trade or is internal reprocessing
Explain why the written booking or work order sets the limit of your authority on site
Apply the stop, record and refer step when a request goes beyond the approved scope

instruction.heading: What this course covers
instruction.body: This course teaches you to clean specialty appliances and machines at the external level and at the level of accessible components. Specialty appliances include commercial dishwashers, commercial ovens and fryers, coffee machines, ice machines, commercial washing machines and dryers, and light-duty workshop machines. For each of these, the in-scope work is the outside of the machine, the surfaces around controls, removable trays and racks, drip trays and grounds bins, door seals and door glass, and any other part that the manufacturer's care instructions say can be cleaned by the user. The cleaning of a surface is the job. Taking a machine apart, reaching inside a housing or changing a part is a different job with different hazards, and it is not covered here. Read the scope every time you start a job, because the same model can be set up differently at different sites.

instruction.heading: What this course excludes, and why
instruction.body: Five kinds of work are excluded. The first is electrical repair and any work inside an electrical enclosure, which needs a licence under state or territory rules. The second is gas appliance servicing, including cleaning or touching burners, igniters, gas valves and flues, which needs a gasfitter or a person registered for that work under the rules of the state or territory. In Victoria, internal cleaning of a Type A unit is covered work for plumbers in the specialised class. The third is refrigerant handling and work on refrigeration circuits. Regulation 111 makes it an offence to do work on RAC equipment without the required licence, and the regulation reads that work broadly (check the current compilation on legislation.gov.au before relying on the wording). The fourth is internal reprocessing, such as opening panels to clean inside, descaling heating elements or boilers, or working on internal fryer oil systems or pumps. The fifth is resetting safety devices such as thermostats, interlocks and tripped switches. Some work near these items is covered elsewhere in the Skilled curriculum, such as domestic oven cleaning in the kitchen group and kitchen exhaust cleaning in commercial and office cleaning. This lesson does not cover those lessons. Each exclusion matters because a worker who opens a housing has taken on a risk the course has not prepared them for, and in some cases has done regulated work without the required licence.

instruction.heading: Authority comes from the booking, not from the person on site
instruction.body: You may clean an appliance only when the owner, operator or site manager has authorised the work. The authority is set by the booking or work order, which should name the equipment, the tasks included, the tasks excluded, and any special conditions. A manager who asks you to do something verbal on site has not changed the booking. You should record the request and get it confirmed in writing before you act on it. If the request is for something outside this course, you must refuse that part, complete any in-scope work that was booked, and report the refusal to your supervisor. Refusing excluded work is not a failure of service. It protects the customer, the worker and the business, and it keeps the record accurate. This applies even when the customer is insistent or the machine appears to be faulty and the customer expects you to fix it.

instruction.heading: Stop, record and refer
instruction.body: When a task is outside scope, or you are unsure whether it is, stop before you touch the item. Record what you saw, what was asked, who asked, and the time. Tell the customer in plain words what you can do under the booking and what needs a different provider. Refer the item to the business's escalation contact for the site or to the owner's nominated service provider. Do not start a partial task to see whether it will work. A partial task on an appliance can leave it unsafe, can void the warranty, and can cause a fault that you then have to explain. If you are unsure about a single component, treat the component as out of scope until the supervisor confirms otherwise.

procedure: Read the full booking or work order before you travel, and note the equipment, the tasks included and the tasks excluded.
On arrival, confirm the named contact and check the equipment list against the booking. Note any extra machines on site.
Identify each appliance you have been asked to clean and classify each requested task as in scope, excluded, or unclear.
For any task that is excluded or unclear, stop before touching the item and record the request with the time and the name of the person who made it.
Explain to the contact what you can do under the booking and what needs another provider. Do not promise repairs or fixes.
Get any change to scope confirmed in writing by the owner or the nominated site contact before you act on it.
Complete the in-scope tasks only, and record which machines were cleaned and which were referred.
Report any refusal or referral to your supervisor at the end of the job, with the reason and the customer's response.

workedExamples.situation: A café owner books the external cleaning of a commercial coffee machine and a commercial dishwasher. On arrival, the owner asks you to take the coffee machine's side panel off so you can clean behind the boiler, because the milk residue there smells sour.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do with the side panel request, and what do you do with the rest of the job?
workedExamples.reasoning: Removing a side panel exposes internal parts, including the boiler and the electrical and water connections on many machines. That is internal work and is outside the course. Refuse the panel removal, record the request and the owner's words, and tell the owner that a service technician can look behind the panel. Continue with the external cleaning of the coffee machine and the full dishwasher exterior, because those tasks are in the booking. Report the refusal and the sour smell to the supervisor so the business can offer the owner a referral.

workedExamples.situation: A commercial fryer is on the booking for an exterior clean. The owner says the fryer's oil is dark and asks you to drain it and replace the filter pad to make the fryer clean inside.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Is draining oil and changing the filter pad in scope, and how do you respond?
workedExamples.reasoning: Draining hot oil and handling the internal filter is work inside the machine, with burn and fire risk, and it is not part of the external clean. Decline it and do not touch the oil. Record the request and tell the owner the oil and filter are for the operator or the fryer's service provider under the site procedure. Complete the external clean, then report the request to the supervisor.

equipmentAndPpe: The written booking or work order, printed or on a device
The site contact's name and the escalation contact recorded in the job
Your business's approved scope list for specialty appliances
Basic personal protective equipment as set by the site and the job, including the gloves and eye protection listed in the business's required PPE field

commonErrors.error: Accepting a verbal request on site and starting work without changing the booking.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop, record the request, and get written confirmation from the owner before you touch the item. A verbal request does not change the booking.

commonErrors.error: Treating the whole machine as in scope because one part of it is cleanable.
commonErrors.prevention: Classify each component separately. The external surface may be in scope while the internal housing is not.

commonErrors.error: Trying a quick fix to show willingness to help, such as resetting a tripped switch or removing a guard.
commonErrors.prevention: Do not reset safety devices or remove guards. Record the fault, describe what you saw, and refer it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The Safe Work Australia model code on managing risks of plant lists appliances within its definition of plant (no page date shown). Appliances are therefore covered by the duty to manage risks, and a worker must not create a new risk by working on an appliance outside their task.
Work on electrical installations, gas appliances and refrigeration systems is regulated work. This lesson does not grant a licence, certificate or authority for any of it.
Completing this lesson does not qualify a worker to clean the inside of any appliance, change parts or work on controls.

qualityStandard: Every task on the job is recorded as in scope, excluded or referred, with a reason
No internal panel, cover, guard or safety device is removed, opened or reset
Any change to the booking is confirmed in writing before work on that item starts
documentationEvidence: The booking or work order with the list of equipment and tasks
A record of each refused or referred task, including the request, the person who made it and the time
The name of the site contact and the supervisor notified at the end of the job
summary: Specialty appliance cleaning covers the outside and accessible parts only, within the owner's authority.
Electrical, gas, refrigerant, internal reprocessing and safety device work are excluded, and they need licensed or authorised trades.
Stop, record and refer whenever a task is outside the booking or unclear.
Completing this course does not grant a licence or authority to do regulated work.

knowledgeChecks.question: A site manager asks you, in person, to clean inside a commercial oven's control housing. The booking only lists the oven's exterior. What is the correct first response?
options: Clean now, because the site manager asked for it in person and an on-site request outranks the written booking details
Decline the internal request, record it with the time and the name of the person who asked, and get written confirmation before any change
Clean inside the housing only if the oven has been switched off and cooled, since that makes internal work safe to carry out on the day
Ask a co-worker whether they have done this before and follow their method for the internal clean without changing the booking

knowledgeChecks.question: Which task is outside the scope of this course?
options: Wiping the outside of a commercial dishwasher with an approved detergent
Cleaning the drip tray and grounds bin of a coffee machine
Replacing a blown fuse inside an appliance's electrical housing
Cleaning the door glass and rubber seal of a commercial oven

knowledgeChecks.question: A tripped safety thermostat is found on a fryer during an external clean. What should the worker do?
options: Reset the thermostat once and test the fryer, so the owner knows it works and no fault needs recording
Remove the back panel to look at what tripped, then test the fryer if nothing looks damaged inside
Turn the fryer on and off until the thermostat resets itself, which usually clears a fault once it cools
Leave the thermostat alone, record the fault, and refer it to the owner's service provider

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the booking or work order primarily establish?
options: The authority for the work, including the included and excluded tasks
The price the customer will pay for any extra work the worker chooses to do
The licence the worker holds for the appliance
The warranty terms the manufacturer has set for the appliance

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must you refuse excluded work even when the customer is insistent?
options: Because the customer cannot pay for extra tasks on the day, so the booking cannot be changed
Because excluded internal work carries risks and may need a licence the worker does not hold
Because the course only allows cleaning on weekdays, and the restriction applies to every booking
Because the supervisor must always attend in person for every appliance clean, whatever the task

officialReferences.covers: Current compilation: the legislation.gov.au version list shows the compilation in force from 1 July 2026 as the latest version, and its contents list regulation 111, 'Carrying out work in relation to RAC equipment'. The regulation 111 text was read in the compilation for 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026: it applies to a person who carries out work in relation to RAC equipment, which includes servicing and maintaining it, unless the person holds a refrigerant handling licence entitled to that work or falls within a listed exception, and contravening it is a strict liability offence. officialReferences.title: Electricians
officialReferences.covers: An electrical licence is needed before any electrical wiring work. Building Commission NSW manages the licence. Publisher: NSW Government (Building Commission NSW).

officialReferences.title: Electrical workers
officialReferences.covers: Energy Safe Victoria licenses electrical workers. Electrical installation work needs a registered electrical contractor. Publisher: Energy Safe Victoria.

officialReferences.title: Gasfitter licences
officialReferences.covers: Names the Building and Plumbing Commission as the body that licenses gasfitters in Victoria. Publisher: Energy Safe Victoria.

officialReferences.title: Classes of electrical work licences
officialReferences.covers: Six licence classes. The open electrical work licence can repair electrical equipment. The page does not name the administering body. Publisher: WorkSafe Queensland.

officialReferences.title: Gasfitting
officialReferences.pageDate: Last published 2 November 2026; last reviewed 31 August 2021
officialReferences.covers: The gasfitting occupational licence is issued by the Chief Gas Examiner and Resources Safety and Health Queensland, not by QBCC. Scope includes servicing a gas system. Publisher: Queensland Building and Construction Commission (page); licence issued by the Chief Gas Examiner.

officialReferences.title: Servicing Type A gas appliances (AS 4575)
officialReferences.covers: Victoria only. Internal cleaning of a Type A appliance is covered work for plumbers in the specialised class. Publisher: Building and Plumbing Commission (Victoria).

officialReferences.title: Electrical licensing
officialReferences.covers: Electrical work is licensed by the Electrical Licensing Board. Its definition of electrical work covers work on appliances powered by electricity. Publisher: Government of Western Australia.

officialReferences.title: Having gasfitting work done
officialReferences.covers: All gasfitting work must be carried out by a licensed gasfitter. Building and Energy issues the licence. Servicing and cleaning are not addressed. Publisher: Government of Western Australia (Building and Energy).

officialReferences.title: Plumbing, gas fitting or electrical contractors licence
officialReferences.covers: Consumer and Business Services administers this licence. It covers electrical work on appliances and gas fitting downstream of the meter. Publisher: Business.gov.au (ABLIS) listing for the South Australian Government.

officialReferences.title: Electrical contractor licence
officialReferences.covers: An electrical contractor licence is needed to contract for electrical work. The page does not name the issuing body and does not cover gas. Publisher: Consumer, Building and Occupational Services (Tasmanian Department of Justice).

officialReferences.title: Electrical licensing contacts
officialReferences.covers: Names the Electrical Safety Regulator within NT WorkSafe. Licence classes are not defined on this page. Publisher: NT WorkSafe (Northern Territory Government).

officialReferences.title: Electrician licence
officialReferences.covers: Electricians must be licensed under the Construction Occupations (Licensing) Act 2004. The page does not name the issuing body. Publisher: ACT Government (ACT Planning).

officialReferences.title: Gas appliance workers
officialReferences.covers: Anyone doing gas appliance work in the ACT must hold a licence. No licence class is named on the page. Publisher: ACT Government (ACT Planning; names Access Canberra).
